title: Internal Hom transport squares for cycles and homology
statement: Let X be a scheme, V an open of X and W an open of V, and F restriction to V followed by localization over W [new-b2-homology-evaluation-definitions]. Suppose e(M,N):F(Hom(M,N))≅Hom(F(M),F(N)) is natural in both module arguments [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For integer cochain complexes T,J and integer n, put A=F(T), K=F(J). There exist internal-Hom comparison isomorphisms b:F(Hom(H^(-n)(T),H^0(J)))≅Hom(H^(-n)(A),H^0(K)), s:F(Hom(Z^(-n)(T),Z^0(J)))≅Hom(Z^(-n)(A),Z^0(K)), t:F(Hom(Z^(-n)(T),J^0))≅Hom(Z^(-n)(A),K^0), and v:F(Hom(Z^(-n)(T),H^0(J)))≅Hom(Z^(-n)(A),H^0(K)). They satisfy F(Hom(T.iCycles,1));t=e(T^(-n),J^0);Hom(A.iCycles,1), F(Hom(1,J.iCycles));t=s;Hom(1,K.iCycles), F(Hom(1,J.homologyPi));v=s;Hom(1,K.homologyPi), and F(Hom(T.homologyPi,1));v=b;Hom(A.homologyPi,1). There is no Hom-complex object or product projection in this statement.

proof.text: The moduleOverFunctor_limits_proof and moduleOverFunctor_colimits_proof localization comparisons, transported by overFunctorEquiv through the open-site equivalence, make F exact. For T and J take the inverse exact-functor cycle and homology comparisons z_L and d_L. Kernel and cokernel universal properties show that z_L commutes with cycle inclusions and that F(homologyπ);d_L=z_L;homologyπ.

Compose e with Hom(z_T inverse,z_J), Hom(z_T inverse,identity), Hom(z_T inverse,d_J), and Hom(d_T inverse,d_J) to define s,t,v,b. The inverse to each comparison is supplied by the inverse object isomorphisms and e inverse. Apply the given e naturality to (T.iCycles,identity), (identity,J.iCycles), (identity,J.homologyπ), and (T.homologyπ,identity). Substitute the inclusion and quotient squares from the preceding step; the intermediate object isomorphisms cancel, giving the four displayed squares. Empty opens and zero complexes satisfy the same universal properties; no boundedness hypothesis is used.

theorem openOver_internalHom_cycle_homology_squares (X : Scheme.{u})
    (V : X.Opens) (W : V.toScheme.Opens)
    (e : ∀ M N : X.Modules,
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
        SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).obj
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) M N) ≅
      SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).obj M)
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).obj N))
    (he : ∀ (M M' N N' : X.Modules) (f : M' ⟶ M) (g : N ⟶ N'),
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
        SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).map
          (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) f g) ≫ (e M' N').hom =
        (e M N).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
            SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).map f)
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
            SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W).map g))
    (T J : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι ⋙
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf W
    let A := (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj T
    let K := (moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor X V W).obj J
    ∃ b : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
          (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0)) ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.homology (-n)) (K.homology 0),
      ∃ s : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
          (T.cycles (-n)) (J.cycles 0)) ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.cycles (-n)) (K.cycles 0),
      ∃ t : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
          (T.cycles (-n)) (J.X 0)) ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.cycles (-n)) (K.X 0),
      ∃ v : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf)
          (T.cycles (-n)) (J.homology 0)) ≅
          SheafOfModules.homObj (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.cycles (-n)) (K.homology 0),
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (T.iCycles (-n)) (𝟙 _)) ≫
            t.hom = (e (T.X (-n)) (J.X 0)).hom ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W)
            (A.iCycles (-n)) (𝟙 _) ∧
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (𝟙 _) (J.iCycles 0)) ≫ t.hom =
          s.hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
            (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (𝟙 _) (K.iCycles 0) ∧
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (𝟙 _) (J.homologyπ 0)) ≫ v.hom =
          s.hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
            (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (𝟙 _) (K.homologyπ 0) ∧
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (T.homologyπ (-n)) (𝟙 _)) ≫
            v.hom = b.hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
              (R := V.toScheme.sheaf.over W) (A.homologyπ (-n)) (𝟙 _)
